Current historical checklist corroborates unfinished packaging, with clean-machine setup, reviewer access, approximately two-minute successful task demo, isolation/live TOTP checks and publication still outstanding: `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/SUBMISSION.md:7-19`. Treat this as a checklist artifact, not proof that none of these were later done.

For “extras,” defensible distinction: polishing the vault dashboard, branding/video/avatar, invitations/delegation, stored personal information, elaborate multi-user/shared-channel UX and provider/proxy experimentation expanded the product. **Recovery, real-site reliability, isolation, revocation, result verification and closing the demo/setup gaps directly support the assignment**, so avoid calling all subsequent work unnecessary.

Nuance for response: **minimal vault UI/revocation and the two-minute demo are required; richer dashboard/sharing, Digital Twin and recording infrastructure are optional. Multi-user privacy enforcement is required once you choose a multi-user implementation.**

No evidence supports saying all later work was unnecessary. Reliability, auth, TOTP, requester isolation, persistent/revocable access, result verification and a successful Google-only chatbot path remain assignment work. Broad experiments become optional only after a small, credible end-to-end acceptance set passes.
